newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda launches new Familia in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Mazda launches new Familia in Japan.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp on Friday launched a partially remodelled Familia compact four-door sedan and three-door hatchback in Japan.
The new Familia model has a monthly sales target of 5,400 cars, Mazda president Henry Wallace said at a press preview of the model.
The domestic selling price of a 1300 cc version with a manual gearbox and without air conditioners will start at 855,000 yen for hatchbacks and 923,000 yen for sedans, he said.
For the new Familia, 1.3-, 1.5-, 1.6- and 1.8-litre gasoline engines and a 1.7-litre diesel engine are available.
Asked if Mazda can achieve the target, Wallace said: "Yes, I do expect the target to be met and I hope our dealers will exceed the target."
Mazda decided to launch the new Familia hatchback as its predecessor, the Familia Neo hatchback, had met with poor demand due to its unique styling, another official said.
Mazda has been posting operating losses since 1993/94 due to poor domestic sales of its mainstay sedan models. It has forecast an operating profit of 20 billion yen in 1996/97, ending next March.
Mazda is owned 33.4 percent by Ford Motor Co.
Asked if the new Familia would help Mazda achieve its overall sales target, Ronald Leight, a senior managing director in charge of sales, said: "It will have a positive effect on full year volume."
In May, Mazda forecast overall domestic sales of 440,000 vehicles in the year to March 1997, up 12.5 percent from a year earlier, and exports of 430,000, up 0.7 percent.
Mazda said its domestic sales fell nine percent in the April-September period from a year earlier to 159,534 units, while exports in the same period rose three percent to 209,100.

Asked if Mazda would launch a completely remodelled Familia in 1998 or 1999 with a shared platform for the car with Ford, Wallace said: "We are obviously working with Ford on how we share a platform, but it won't affect the present product cycle plan we are going through."

On developing synergy between Mazda and Ford on sharing components and complementing each other in emerging markets, Wallace said: "We are still in the planning stage, but we are making good progress on that."
